requirement: Describe the study as a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled parallel superiority trial of active versus sham transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation for analgesia during outpatient endometrial biopsy.

evidence.text: The protocol describes random assignment to active or placebo TENS, participant and provider blinding and outpatient biopsy.
The plan explicitly calls the comparison a superiority trial.

requirement: Define the eligible population as adults at least 18 years old undergoing outpatient endometrial biopsy at participating Duke gynecology sites, excluding inability to follow or adjust TENS, damaged application skin, electronic implanted devices, inability to consent, prior TENS experience, concurrent procedures and pregnancy.

evidence.text: The protocol lists adult outpatient-biopsy eligibility and the TENS, consent, concurrent-procedure and pregnancy exclusions.

requirement: Define active TENS as four pads at T10-L1 and S2-S4 with all four electrodes connected and intensity increased to the maximum nonpainful sensory level; define sham as the same device and pads but only two electrodes connected, starting 5 minutes before biopsy and ending 5 minutes after.
acceptable_values: four pads at T10-L1 and S2-S4

evidence.text: The intervention section specifies pad location, connection pattern, intensity and procedure timing for active and sham devices.

requirement: Specify the REDCap randomization sequence, block sizes or variation, allocation ratio, stratification by site or preprocedure analgesic use if any, concealment and authorized access; do not treat the protocol's expectation of adequate block balance as a complete randomization specification.

evidence.text: The protocol says REDCap uses a statistician-provided schema and mentions block randomization but omits ratio, block and concealment details.

requirement: State that participants and biopsy providers are masked while the coordinator who places, teaches and operates TENS is unmasked, and evaluate masking success from participant and provider treatment guesses without using those guesses to redefine the primary population.
acceptable_values: masking assessment separate from primary population

evidence.text: The protocol identifies masked participants/providers, the unmasked coordinator and postprocedure treatment guesses.

requirement: Define the primary endpoint as participant-reported pain immediately after endometrial biopsy on a 0-to-100 mm visual analogue scale, with lower scores indicating less pain; distinguish it from pain collected during the biopsy or at other procedure intervals.

evidence.text: The protocol defines the VAS range and collects pain at multiple procedure times but uses broad wording for pain at biopsy.
The plan identifies pain immediately after biopsy as the primary outcome.

requirement: Resolve the reference's requirement to adjust for baseline pain even though the protocol identifies a preprocedure anxiety VAS but no clear preprocedure pain VAS; define the baseline-pain source and timing or remove the unsupported covariate before unblinding.
acceptable_values: covariate retained only if prespecified and observed

evidence.text: The protocol explicitly measures preprocedure anxiety but does not clearly identify a baseline pain score.
The planned primary linear regression adjusts for baseline pain.

requirement: Compare primary post-biopsy VAS between assigned treatment arms using linear regression, report the adjusted active-minus-sham mean difference with a two-sided 95% confidence interval and p-value, and prespecify the baseline-pain covariate resolution and any site or preprocedure-analgesic adjustment.

evidence.text: The plan specifies linear regression adjusting for baseline pain and two-sided alpha 0.05, but not the reported contrast or other covariates.

requirement: Test the two-sided superiority null of no difference in mean immediate post-biopsy VAS against an active-versus-sham difference at alpha 0.05, while interpreting direction so lower active-arm VAS favors TENS.
acceptable_values: superiority null of no mean difference

evidence.text: The protocol hypothesizes lower pain in the active group.
The plan defines superiority and two-tailed significance level 0.05.

requirement: Define the primary analysis set as all randomized participants analyzed as assigned and specify rules for canceled or incomplete biopsy, device nonactivation or disconnection, crossover, inability to provide the immediate VAS and postrandomization withdrawal.

evidence.text: The protocol defines randomization, intervention and withdrawal rights but no efficacy analysis population.

requirement: Define the primary estimand using all randomized eligible participants, assigned active versus sham TENS, immediate post-biopsy VAS and a mean-difference contrast, with strategies for device failure, participant intensity changes, additional analgesic use, incomplete biopsy and missing pain assessment.

evidence.text: The protocol permits participant-controlled intensity and standard-care analgesics but does not formalize intercurrent-event handling.

requirement: Predefine missing primary and repeated VAS handling, report availability and reasons by arm and timepoint, and conduct a sensitivity analysis compatible with the primary estimand rather than restricting silently to complete procedures.

evidence.text: Multiple pain and survey measurements are collected, but neither source defines missing-data handling.

requirement: Use the prospective target of 160 consented/randomized participants: 128 evaluable participants, 64 per arm, provide 80% power at two-sided alpha 0.05 to detect a 15 mm difference assuming 30 mm standard deviation, inflated by 20% attrition; do not substitute actual enrollment of 149.

evidence.text: The protocol prospectively targets 160 participants.
The plan provides the 15 mm effect, 30 mm SD, 64 per arm, 80% power and 20% attrition assumptions.

requirement: Analyze pain VAS at speculum placement, tenaculum placement, removal of speculum, 5 minutes and 15 minutes after biopsy as time-specific secondary outcomes, and prespecify whether a longitudinal repeated-measures model or separate timepoint models are used.

evidence.text: The protocol identifies the repeated procedural pain times as secondary measures.

requirement: Define scoring and direction for patient tolerability and acceptability, willingness to choose the same pain control, provider ease/satisfaction and perceived patient pain, and report arm contrasts with valid denominators and confidence intervals.

evidence.text: The postprocedure surveys include tolerability, acceptability, future choice and provider ratings without complete scoring or analysis rules.

requirement: Prespecify exploratory associations of pain with preprocedure anxiety, concomitant analgesic or anxiolytic use, prior biopsy, sociodemographic factors and site, including covariate coding, functional forms and an explicit distinction from randomized treatment-effect estimation.

evidence.text: The protocol proposes correlations between pain and anxiety, medication and sociodemographic factors and includes more than one Duke location.

requirement: Keep immediate post-biopsy pain as the sole confirmatory endpoint and define multiplicity handling or exploratory labeling for repeated pain times, acceptability, tolerability, provider ratings, masking checks and covariate/subgroup analyses.

evidence.text: The protocol lists many secondary pain, survey and correlation outcomes without multiplicity rules.
The reference gives a common 0.05 level but no familywise strategy.

requirement: Include sensitivity analyses for preprocedure analgesic use, site, masking guess, actual device activation/connectivity and influential or bounded VAS observations, while preserving randomized assignment as the primary contrast.

evidence.text: Analgesic use, multiple sites, masking guesses and device operation may affect observed pain, but no sensitivity analyses are defined.

requirement: Analyze safety among participants who begin assigned device use, summarizing postprocedure syncope, heavy bleeding, TENS reaction and other adverse events for one week by received treatment, severity, seriousness, relationship, withdrawal and outcome; list related hospitalization or death separately.

evidence.text: The protocol specifies one-week tracking for syncope, heavy bleeding and TENS reactions, ongoing PI review and immediate reporting of related hospitalization or death.

requirement: Before release, confirm from Duke IRB history that matching Version 1.9 protocol and analysis plan dated 2023-08-23 were finalized without access to randomized outcomes: they postdate the 2022-12-13 study start and are only four months before completion; exclude the family if the amendment used observed treatment or outcome data.

evidence.text: The protocol visibly identifies Version 1.9 and approval date 2023-08-23.
The one-page analysis plan carries the same IRB, NCT, Version 1.9 and date.

requirement: Keep the one-page reference plan annotation-only: the model-visible protocol may expose design, VAS times, target and broad between-arm intent, but must not expose the reference-only 15 mm effect, 30 mm SD, 64-per-arm power calculation or baseline-adjusted linear regression.
acceptable_values: reference-only power and model not visible

evidence.text: Full visual review found the design, target and broad pain comparison but not the reference's numerical power inputs or primary regression.
The independent reference contains the effect, SD, power and regression choices.
